title: Prompt Maker: let a free GPT turn one-line bad prompts into usable ones
summary: Ruben Hassid argues you can skip learning prompt engineering by running a rough one-liner through his free "Prompt Maker" GPT, then pasting the output into a fresh chat. He shows the two-step workflow with LinkedIn hooks and newsletter ideation, and ends with a simple newsletter growth ask.

principles.text: Output quality is capped by input quality, so fix the prompt first.
principles.quote: You know ChatGPT is as good as the input ( = the prompt).

principles.text: Don't aim for a perfect prompt; a decent start from a terrible one-liner is the practical win.
principles.quote:
Is it the best prompt possible for such task? No.

Is it a fantastic start from a one-liner terrible prompt? The best you could have.

principles.text: Use a two-step workflow: generate a better prompt, then run it in a fresh chat with your own content.
principles.quote: From your bad prompt → to the Prompt Maker → to a better prompt to copy.

principles.text: Fence off your own input with delimiters so the model knows what is data versus instruction.
Run the same prompt across different models to get different twists, and pick the strongest for the task.
principles.quote: You want a different twist? Select another model to write (GPT-4.5 is also good).

principles.text: Ask readers to forward the newsletter; a 1% forward rate on a large list adds meaningful free growth.
principles.quote: If 1% of you forward this email to a colleague, that’s an extra 4,000 people to keep this newsletter free forever!
